title: Studio Autonomous Page Draft
subtitle: A Studio-specific working shape for producing a page draft whose source graph, text, images, and review evidence cohere.
scope: One Studio story page moving through autonomous draft mode with source repair, text drafting, image generation, visual inspection, and human review.
sourceCoverage: Template only; replace placeholder Studio page, beat, prompt, asset, command, and review references with real sources from the current run.

templateMeta.useWhen: Use this when a Studio page is being produced through autonomous draft mode and the work must not skip source graph completeness, coherence judgment, image inspection, or human-review boundaries.
templateMeta.operatingThesis: Treat a Studio draft page as a source/output coherence system: text, images, prompts, source data, monitor logs, and review evidence must explain each other before the draft can be called high quality.
notFor: asset inventories that only list files
final art approval without source lineage

semanticDefinition.objectiveRole: Keep Studio autonomous page drafting from skipping source graph completeness, coherence judgment, image inspection, or human-review boundaries.
semanticDefinition.templateSubtitle: A Studio-specific working shape for producing a page draft whose source graph, text, images, and review evidence cohere.
semanticDefinition.templateScope: One Studio story page moving through autonomous draft mode with source repair, text drafting, image generation, visual inspection, and human review.
semanticDefinition.templateObjective: Produce a high-quality Studio page draft by making the source graph complete enough, drafting the required text, generating or iterating the required images, and recording the coherence and verification evidence before any completion claim.
semanticDefinition.templateSuccessCondition: The page has the target draft text and image outputs, every source/output relationship needed for quality is explicit, the coherence pass is coherent, visual assessment is draft-ready, and human final review remains clearly marked as required.

sections.title: Status Snapshot
sections.role: Summarize page draft state without replacing the source graph, coherence, visual, verification, or tooling evidence.
sections.rationale: The page needs one quick state signal, but the evidence that supports it must stay in the sections below.

sections.title: Source Graph Completeness
sections.role: Track whether page and beat source data is explicit enough to support high-quality text and image drafting.
sections.rationale: Missing cinematic directions, facts, reference assets, prompt lineage, or output paths are quality blockers when they control the draft.

sections.title: Draft Coherence Pass
sections.role: Record the performed reasoning pass that compares source graph, prompts, text, images, and page sequence.
sections.rationale: A page is not done because assets exist; coherence must be judged and recorded against the explicit source graph.

sections.title: Visual Page Draft Assessment
sections.role: Inspect actual image files panel by panel and judge whether the page works as a visual sequence.
sections.rationale: Visual draft quality requires opening the generated assets and checking them against page, beat, and sequence intent.

sections.title: Verification Checkpoints
sections.role: Track the concrete checks that prove the final draft-mode state was inspected after repair and generation.
sections.rationale: Completion claims need repeatable checks such as work-page, visual inspection, monitor review, and rendered page review.

sections.title: Tooling Surface
sections.role: Expose the Studio tools, Codex skill, MCP instruments, CLI fallbacks, and monitor surfaces used to operate the draft loop.
sections.rationale: A future run must be able to reproduce how source repair, draft registration, image generation, monitoring, and verification were performed.

draft-coherence-pass.description: A recorded reasoning pass that compares source graph, prompts, generated images, text, and page sequence before a draft completion claim. Each card is a performed coherence judgment with findings, rejections, repairs, and the evidence used.
draft-coherence-pass.structuralContract: Two-column card grid. Each card is one coherence pass over a page or page slice. It must name the source graph snapshot, output artifacts, checks performed, mismatches found, repairs made or required, and the resulting coherence verdict.
notFor: static listing of source fields without performed judgment (use source-graph-completeness)
pixel-only visual judgment without source graph comparison (use visual-page-draft-assessment)

promptGuidance.operatingThesis: Treat coherence as an action that must be performed and recorded. A draft is coherent only when source graph, prompts, text, images, and sequence support the same page intent. If any source edge, prompt, image, or sequence element contradicts the objective, the pass must require repair or regeneration.
keepDistinct: rejections and why they were rejected
inspect: Read source graph completeness before judging outputs.
Open actual image files and compare them to beat/page source data.
Compare prompts to explicit factRefs, referenceAssetRefs, and cinematic directions.
Compare each panel to neighboring panels and page-level sequence role.
Do not accept a good-looking asset if it is unsupported by the source graph or contradicts the sequence.
update: Create a new card for each substantial coherence pass or iteration.
Set verdict from the worst unresolved coherence failure.
List rejected artifacts with concrete rejection reasons.
List repairs performed and repairs still required separately.
Only set coherent after the pass can point to source graph, output, and visual evidence.
avoid: Do not invent a distinction between high-quality draft and full coherence.
Do not treat final image generation success as coherence proof.
Do not skip source data because the rendered result looks plausible.
Do not bury contradictions as soft gaps when they block the objective.
Do not claim completion without a recorded pass.

aiActions.name: Run draft coherence pass
aiActions.description: Compare source graph, prompts, text, images, and sequence; record mismatches, rejected artifacts, repairs, remaining blockers, and the coherence verdict.

aiActions.name: Derive next repair
aiActions.description: From the coherence failures, choose the next source edit, prompt repair, or image regeneration that moves the whole page toward coherent draft quality.

source-graph-completeness.description: A production-quality surface for checking whether a page or beat has the source graph needed to support a high-quality draft: page intent, beat intent, cinematic directions, fact grounding, reference assets, prompt lineage, output paths, and audit state. This prevents generated output from being treated as complete while the source data needed to explain and reproduce it is missing.
source-graph-completeness.structuralContract: Two-column card grid. Each card represents one page, beat, or page-slice source graph. The card must list required source fields, present values, missing or drifted graph edges, blocking quality gaps, and the repair action needed before a draft can be called coherent.
notFor: visual review of actual image pixels (use visual-page-draft-assessment)
the performed reasoning pass comparing source to output (use draft-coherence-pass)
final proof evidence after all checks are done (use verification or proof types)

promptGuidance.operatingThesis: Treat missing source data as a quality blocker when that data controls image generation, text generation, or page coherence. The source graph is complete only when page intent, beat intent, cinematic direction, facts, references, prompts, outputs, and audit state are explicit enough for another agent or human to understand why the draft looks the way it does.
keepDistinct: factRefs and the facts they ground
audit warnings/errors and whether they are quality blockers
repair action required before generation or completion claim
inspect: Check the page structure before looking at image beauty.
Verify that every beat has the explicit facts and references its prompt or image depends on.
Verify that every generated or selected image has a prompt lineage and output path tied back to the beat.
Treat work-page soft labels as potentially blocking when they affect draft quality.
Mark drift when source fields, prompts, images, and audit state disagree.
update: Use one card per page or beat source graph, depending on document scope.
Set status from the worst unresolved graph blocker.
Write missingEdges as concrete fields or relationships, not vague prose.
Write requiredRepair as the next source edit needed before the page can be judged coherent.
Update after every generation or manual source edit.
avoid: Do not call source graph complete because images exist.
Do not downgrade missing factRefs, referenceAssetRefs, or cinematic directions to harmless notes when they affect generation quality.
Do not hide missing graph data under generic audit wording.
Do not infer invisible source state from a good-looking image; write the graph edge explicitly.

aiActions.name: Complete source graph
aiActions.description: Inspect the page/beat source graph, identify missing grounding, direction, reference, prompt, and output edges, then propose the required source edits before draft completion.

aiActions.name: Classify quality blockers
aiActions.description: Reclassify audit gaps according to the current objective, marking fields as blocking when they control draft quality even if another system labels them soft.

status-snapshot.name: Status Snapshot
status-snapshot.description: A summary section that compresses the current document into top-level counts and distribution signals.
status-snapshot.structuralContract: Stats-first section with snapshot cards and no item grid requirement. Use for high-level totals and state distribution, not for individual entities.

promptGuidance.operatingThesis: Treat the section as document-wide compression, not as an item inventory.
inspect: Read the rest of the document before changing snapshot stats.
update: Recompute stats and callout language from the current section set and payload.
avoid: Do not add individual work items here.

tooling-surface.name: Tooling Surface
tooling-surface.description: An operational tooling surface that collects the skills, scripts, workflows, and local instruments used to inspect, verify, or modify the domain without treating them as source material.
tooling-surface.structuralContract: Two-column card grid of tooling-status items. Each item should represent one operational instrument with clear purpose, invocation, and caveats. Use when the section is about how the domain is worked on rather than what the domain says.

promptGuidance.operatingThesis: Treat the section as the operational instrument layer used to inspect, verify, modify, or refresh the domain.
inspect: Check whether each tool is currently trusted, caveated, prototype, broken, or missing.
update: Keep purpose, when-to-use, invocation, and caveats explicit for each tool.
avoid: Do not treat tooling entries as primary source material or domain claims.

verification-checkpoints.name: Verification Checkpoints
verification-checkpoints.description: Compact verification section for a small set of checks, probes, or repair validations.
verification-checkpoints.structuralContract: One-column card grid of probe-status items. Use when the verification surface is checkpoint-like rather than evidence-rich.
notFor: full verification surfaces with coverage and gaps

promptGuidance.operatingThesis: Treat the section as a compact list of checks or repair validations.
inspect: Check the latest result or ticket state for each checkpoint before updating status.
update: Keep each checkpoint short and action-oriented.
avoid: Do not turn checkpoints into evidence-rich verification surfaces or proof ladders.

visual-page-draft-assessment.description: A visual judgment and repair surface for a drafted story page. Each card compares page intent, panel specifications, actual images, text state, sequence rhythm, violations, and the next repair action so image existence does not masquerade as visual draft completeness.
visual-page-draft-assessment.structuralContract: Two-column card grid. Each card is one page-level assessment with panel-by-panel verdicts, sequence assessment, text/source state, violations, repair priority, and next action. Use this after autonomous or manual page drafting when the question is whether the page is visually usable as a draft, not merely whether files exist.
notFor: generic production readiness without visual inspection (use readiness or acceptance criteria sections)
asset inventories that only list image paths
final art approval without page/sequence context

promptGuidance.operatingThesis: Treat the card as a page-quality assessment, not a file-presence check. The page is draft-ready only when the text/source state, each panel image, and the page sequence cohere with the stated page intent and panel specs.
keepDistinct: sequence-level rhythm, mirror, through-line, and continuity assessment
inspect: Open every existing image path before marking a panel keep or draft-ready.
Compare actual pixels against imageBrief, directionNote, panelRole, cinematicDirections, page compositionArc, throughLine, mirroringPairs, and cinematicNotes.
Assess the page as a sequence, not only as three isolated panels.
Look for forbidden image features: captions, speech bubbles, UI text, page borders, faux paper, stock/photo-realism when an illustration is required, and generic imagery that misses the beat.
If generation or inspection tooling fails, mark blocked-by-tooling or usable-with-risks rather than draft-ready.
update: Use one card per page assessment pass or update the current card when the assessment is still the active draft state.
Set verdict from the worst meaningful page blocker, not from the best panel.
Write panelAssessments as concrete observations with beatId, imagePath, specSummary, actualObservation, verdict, violations, and repairPromptDelta.
Write sequenceAssessment after panel assessments so it reflects actual page rhythm.
Make nextAction the first repair that improves the page sequence, not necessarily the first missing asset.
avoid: Do not count imagePath existence as visual completion.
Do not mark a panel keep without visual inspection or an explicit draft-risk caveat.
Do not hide quality failures under generic audit warnings.
Do not regenerate dependent panels before repairing an upstream panel that anchors the sequence.
Do not confuse draft-ready with final human approval.

aiActions.name: Review page images against spec
aiActions.description: Open the referenced images, compare them to page and panel specifications, update panel verdicts, and propose the next repair action.

aiActions.name: Propose repair order
aiActions.description: Given panel verdicts and sequence dependencies, choose the first image or source repair that best improves the page as a sequence.

relationships.rationale: Draft status should summarize the current source graph state instead of hiding source blockers.
The coherence pass must judge the draft against the explicit page and beat source graph.

evidence.description: A coherence pass should identify the source graph, prompts, beats, and images it judged.

relationships.rationale: Coherence cannot be claimed without panel-by-panel visual inspection of actual assets.
A draft-ready visual judgment needs concrete checks that can be rerun or audited.
The source graph and draft loop are operational only when the Studio tools and skill paths are visible.
Verification checkpoints need the tool or command that produced the evidence.

stageSignals.when: source-graph-completeness has no page or beat card
stageSignals.question: Which Studio page and beats are being drafted, and what source graph is currently missing?

stageSignals.when: source graph exists but draft-coherence-pass has no corresponding performed judgment
stageSignals.question: What source, prompt, text, image, and sequence comparison has actually been performed?

stageSignals.when: coherence pass exists but visual-page-draft-assessment has not inspected the actual image files
stageSignals.question: Which actual images were opened and judged against the page and beat specification?

stageSignals.when: visual assessment exists but verification-checkpoints do not cover the final draft-mode checks
stageSignals.question: Which concrete checks prove the page state, images, monitor logs, and human-review boundary?

stageSignals.when: source graph, coherence pass, visual assessment, verification, and tooling are populated and linked
stageSignals.question: Is the page a high-quality draft with human final review still explicit?

validOperations.label: Add source graph card
validOperations.description: Add or update the page/beat source graph card with required fields, present fields, missing edges, quality blockers, and required repair.

validOperations.label: Add coherence pass
validOperations.description: Record a performed comparison of source graph, prompts, text, images, and page sequence.

validOperations.label: Add visual assessment
validOperations.description: Record panel-by-panel visual inspection and the page sequence verdict.

validOperations.label: Add draft verification
validOperations.description: Add a checkpoint for final work-page, monitor, visual, rendered-page, or human-review-boundary evidence.

validOperations.label: Link Studio tooling
validOperations.description: Add or update tool cards for the autonomous drafting skill, MCP tools, CLI fallback, image generation, monitor endpoint, and renderer.

items: Use this section only as the short state summary.

sections.title: Source Graph Completeness

data.name: Studio page source graph
data.scope: One Studio page and its panel beats.
data.requiredGraph: Page intent, page composition arc, beat intents, cinematic directions, factRefs, referenceAssetRefs, prompt lineage, image outputs, work-page report, and audit state.
data.presentGraph: Replace this placeholder with the current page and beat source data before judging output quality.
data.requiredRepair: Fill missing grounding, direction, references, and lineage before claiming the draft coherent.
missingEdges: Replace placeholder beat IDs with real beat IDs.
Record every missing factRef, referenceAssetRef, cinematic direction, prompt ID, and output path that affects draft quality.
driftSignals: Record source/prompt/image/text mismatches here after each generation or manual edit.
qualityBlockers: Missing source fields that control text, image, or sequence quality are blockers, not soft gaps.
auditEvidence: Add the final work-page report and relevant storyboard/continuity audit findings.

sections.rationale: Missing cinematic directions, facts, reference assets, prompt lineage, or output paths are quality blockers when they control the draft.

sections.title: Draft Coherence Pass

data.name: Page draft coherence pass
data.scope: One performed reasoning pass over the current page draft.
data.sourceSnapshot: Summarize the exact source graph snapshot used for this pass.
data.coherenceFinding: Replace this with the comparison of source graph, prompts, text, images, and sequence.
data.nextRepair: Name the first source edit, prompt repair, or image regeneration needed before the verdict can become coherent.
checksPerformed: Compare page intent to all beat intents.
Compare facts and reference assets to prompts and images.
Compare text and images to the page sequence role.
Reject assets that look plausible but do not match the source graph.
artifactAssessments: Record text IDs, image paths, job IDs, prompt IDs, and verdicts.
remainingBlockers: Any missing source data or output/source contradiction that affects quality.

sections.rationale: A page is not done because assets exist; coherence must be judged and recorded against the explicit source graph.

sections.title: Visual Page Draft Assessment

data.name: Page visual draft assessment
data.targetOutput: Three visually acceptable draft images that cohere with the page intent, beat specifications, and adjacent panels.
data.pageIntent: Replace this with the page-level intent and composition arc.
data.sequenceAssessment: Record whether the panels work together as a page, not only as separate images.
data.nextAction: Name the first visual or source repair that improves the page as a sequence.
panelAssessments: For each beat: imagePath, spec summary, actual observation, verdict, violations, and repairPromptDelta.
violations: Record text in image, generic imagery, wrong style, wrong subject, missing through-line, continuity break, or unsupported detail.
repairPriority: Repair upstream source/prompt/image blockers before dependent panel polish.
draftRisks: Human final review is still required even after draft-ready.
imageReviewEvidence: Record how each image was opened or inspected.

sections.rationale: Visual draft quality requires opening the generated assets and checking them against page, beat, and sequence intent.

sections.title: Verification Checkpoints

data.name: Final work-page report
notes: Run work_page after source repair, text registration, and image generation; record remaining warnings as blockers when they affect quality.

data.name: Image generation monitor review
notes: Review image_generation_monitor or monitor endpoint evidence for each live generation job.

data.name: Human final review boundary
notes: State explicitly that the autonomous run produced draft-mode text and images and did not replace human final approval.

sections.rationale: Completion claims need repeatable checks such as work-page, visual inspection, monitor review, and rendered page review.

sections.title: Tooling Surface

data.name: Studio autonomous page draft skill
data.purpose: Operate the Studio autonomous page drafting loop using MCP tools or CLI fallback while preserving source graph, coherence, visual inspection, and human-review boundaries.
data.whenToUse: Use when Codex is asked to make a Studio page draft, complete a page in draft mode, or operate autonomous_page_draft.
data.invocation: Use the skill in Codex; fallback commands are `studio autonomous-draft <pageId>` and `studio work-page <pageId>`.
caveats: The skill performs inference reasoning; the MCP tool only packages state and operations.

data.name: Studio autonomous draft instrument
data.purpose: Package page state, source draft requests, text draft requests, image review/generation requests, audit inputs, and human review checklist.
data.whenToUse: Call first for the page run and again after source edits, text registration, or image generation.
caveats: The instrument does not supply inference reasoning or quality judgment by itself.

data.name: Image generation monitor
data.purpose: Expose live nested Codex image-generation activity so the drafting run can watch inference progress during long jobs.
data.whenToUse: Poll during every live image job until completion, concrete failure, or user stop.
caveats: Do not impose a fixed timeout; judge by monitor activity and concrete failure signals.

objective: Produce a high-quality Studio page draft by making the source graph complete enough, drafting the required text, generating or iterating the required images, and recording the coherence and verification evidence before any completion claim.
successCondition: The page has the target draft text and image outputs, every source/output relationship needed for quality is explicit, the coherence pass is coherent, visual assessment is draft-ready, and human final review remains clearly marked as required.
